[LEXP.7.14.1] `>>` is **arithmetic shift** (sign-preserving):
$a \gg n = \lfloor a / 2^n \rfloor$. `<<` is the shift the other way,
$a \ll n = a \cdot 2^n$ under the `Int` wrap of [LEXP.7.13.1].

The count is never reduced modulo 64. A count of 64 or more therefore gives
`0` or `-1` for `>>` (by the sign of `a`) and `0` for `<<`. A count that is
negative at run time is a trap, a `ComputationError` of kind `DOMAIN`
([LERR.1.4.1]); a negative literal count is refused at compile time
([LEXP.7.8]).
